title: Children's Picnic Sets Recalled by Mervyn's
summary: The paint on the bag contains high levels of lead that violates the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Act. Lead poisoning in children is associated with behavior problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation. Units: About 1,200.

title: Grinders Recalled by S-B Power Tool
summary: Some grinders were shipped without the side handle, which is used to control and guide the tool. Use of the grinder without the side handle can cause consumers to lose control of the tool and be injured. Units: About 920.

title: CPSC, Jetmax International Ltd. Announce Recall to Repair Children's Rocking Chairs Sold at Target Stores
summary: The rear legs of the chair can separate from the rocker's base, causing it to collapse, and the child seated in the chair can fall. Units: About 48,000.

title: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall to Repair Tot Wheels® Entertainer® Infant Walkers
summary: These walkers can collapse unexpectedly during use and injure infants. Units: About 31,000.

title: CPSC, Ace Hardware Corp. Announce Recall of Vinyl Window Blinds
summary: These blinds contain lead exceeding government guidelines, and do not have required labeling warning they contain lead. Over time, vinyl deteriorates from exposure to sunlight and heat, forming lead dust on the surface of the blind. Young children can ingest lead by wiping their hands on the blinds

title: Playtex Products Voluntarily Announces Pacifier Recall in Cooperation with CPSC
summary: Because the latex is aging faster than normal, the nipple can detach from the shield, presenting a choking hazard to babies. Units: About 1.8 million.

title: CPSC, Federated Department Stores Announce Recall of Children's Robes
summary: These robes, when used as sleepwear, fail to meet federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear. title: CPSC, Promotional Resources Group Announce Recall of Bug Zapper Toys Sold With Children's Meals
summary: The balloon tongue on this toy can detach, posing a choking and aspiration hazard to young children. Units: About 105,000.

title: Infant Cargo Skirts Recalled by Associated Merchandising Corp.
summary: The snaps on the panty of these skirts can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 9,500.

title: Sweatshirts Recalled by Jordache Ltd.
summary: The sweatshirts, which fail to meet federal mandatory standards for fabric flammability, could ignite easily and present a serious risk of burn injuries, in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act. Fabrics that do not comply with the standard typically burn faster than newspaper. Units: About

title: CPSC, Kellogg Company Announce Recall of Toy Cars Inside Boxes of Cereal
summary: The tires can detach from the wheels of these cars, posing a choking hazard for young children. Units: 837,000.

title: CPSC, Whitehall-Robins Healthcare Announce Recall of Teething Rings
summary: When bent, these teething rings can fit into an infant's mouth and trigger a gagging reflex. This poses a risk of vomiting, which could result in choking and aspiration. Units: About 475,000.

title: CPSC and Tanaka Announce Recall of Hedge Trimmers and Augers
summary: The fuel tank vents on these products can leak, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 7,500 hedge trimmers and 1,400 augers.

title: CPSC, Apollo Presentation Products Announce Recall of Light Boxes
summary: The light boxes have loose wires and lack adequate grounding, presenting fire, electrocution and shock hazards to consumers. Units: About 30,000.

title: CPSC, Galoob Toys Inc. Announce Recall of Sky Dancers® Flying Dolls
summary: The hard plastic Sky Dancers® dolls can fly rapidly in unpredictable directions, and can hit and injure both children and adults. Units: About 8.9 million.

title: CPSC, Today's Kids Announce Recall of Spinning Ride Toys
summary: The center column can break, causing a child to suddenly fall backward or be hit in the face by the broken column. Units: About 103,000.

title: CPSC, Vtech Industries Announce Recall of Toy Baby Phone
summary: The toy phones have a ball-shaped antenna, which can detach, presenting a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 34,000.
